task.description: WF-02 Step 2c (SECURITY-REVIEWER) for REQ-038 on branch feature/WF02-REQ-038, commit 458101d. Independent re-derivation (not trust of BACKEND-DEV/REVIEWER's claims) of security-invariants.md S1, S4, S7, S8 against the invite-code redemption diff, with hard focus on AC2 (personal-code identity refusal) and AC4 (atomic used_count under concurrency).
acceptance_criteria: S4 identity check: redeemInviteCode's not-yours refusal traced line-by-line; negative scenario (code issued to A, redeemed by B) constructed by reading the code path, confirmed no registration write and no used_count change
S4/S7 atomic used_count: invite_codes row locked FOR UPDATE before the uses-remain check, and check+increment+registration write all inside one transaction with no gap
Identity-leakage tradeoff re-verified independently against the actual unique-index exact-match lookup mechanism
S1: zero DB writes before consent on the i_ deep-link path, traced in resolveInviteDeepLink
S7: valid code on a full event still waitlists, does not override capacity
S8: exactly one AuditLog row per successful redemption, none on refusal
No second code generator, no schema/migration change, no Wishlist artefact

result.summary:
Re-derived every applicable security-invariants.md item against the actual code in apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/registrationReply.ts and the i18n catalogs, plus a direct schema read. All findings below are from tracing the code myself, not from BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's summaries.

1) S4 IDENTITY CHECK (AC2) -- traced hard, negative case constructed. redeemInviteCode (inviteCode.ts:616-826): step 2 does an UNLOCKED precheck by code string (getInviteCodeByCode, exact eq() on the unique-indexed `code` column) purely to fail fast on unknown; step 5 then re-reads the SAME row `.for("update")` by id -- this is the row whose fields feed the decision, never the unlocked precheck. validateInviteCodeForRedemption (inviteCode.ts:572-594) row 4: `issuedToUserId !== null && issuedToUserId !== redeemerUserId` -> `{ ok:false, reason:"not-yours" }`. Constructed the attacker scenario by hand: issuePersonalInviteCode sets issuedToUserId = targetUserId (A) at issuance (inviteCode.ts:196-204); if redeemerUserId = B != A, row 4 fires. Trace forward from that branch (inviteCode.ts:694-705): the switch returns `{ kind: "invite-code-not-yours" }` and RETURNS OUT OF THE TRANSACTION CALLBACK immediately -- step 7 onward (existing-registration read, seats read, decideRegistrationOutcome, the registrations INSERT/UPDATE, the used_count UPDATE at line 797-800, and the writeAuditLog call at 806-818) are all textually BELOW this return and are never reached. Because the whole thing runs inside `db.transaction(...)`, and the only statements executed before the early return are two SELECT ... FOR UPDATE reads (both non-mutating), the transaction has nothing to commit; a rollback or a commit-of-reads-only both leave `registrations` and `invite_codes.used_count` byte-identical to before the call. This satisfies AC2's exact requirement: refused, no registration row, used_count unchanged -- verified by code inspection of the actual control flow, not by running it, but the control flow admits no other path (no write statement anywhere between the entry and this return).

2) S4/S7 ATOMIC used_count (AC4) -- locking scope traced exactly. The `events` row is locked FOR UPDATE first (step 4, line 638-654) -- this alone would NOT serialize two redeemers of the SAME code against DIFFERENT target events sharing nothing, but that is irrelevant to AC4 (same code, same event, by construction). The load-bearing lock is step 5 (line 662-673): `SELECT ... FROM invite_codes WHERE id = precheck.id FOR UPDATE` -- taken INSIDE the same `db.transaction` the events lock and every subsequent statement share. Postgres semantics: a second concurrent transaction's own `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` against the same invite_codes row blocks until the first transaction commits or rolls back, then reads that row's POST-write state (own used_count, freshly re-fetched, no snapshot staleness for a row lock read under READ COMMITTED, which this codebase uses elsewhere per its own transaction discipline). The uses-remain check (validateInviteCodeForRedemption row 2, `usedCount >= maxUses`) runs against `codeRow.usedCount`, i.e. the value read AT STEP 5, AFTER the lock is held -- not a pre-transaction value, not the step-2 precheck's value. The increment (line 797-800, `usedCount: codeRow.usedCount + 1`) and the registrations write (752-781) and the AuditLog write (806-818) are all executed on the SAME `tx` handle, inside the SAME transaction callback, with no `await` outside `tx` between the lock (step 5) and the commit (the function's return, which is the transaction's implicit commit point). There is no gap: the lock is acquired before the check, held through the check, the write, and the increment, and released only at commit -- a second redeemer's lock acquisition cannot interleave a read of used_count into that window. Concretely for the last-use race: redeemer 1 locks, sees usedCount = maxUses-1, passes the check, commits with usedCount=maxUses. Redeemer 2's own FOR UPDATE blocks until 1 commits, then reads usedCount=maxUses fresh, fails the check (`usedCount >= maxUses`), returns invite-code-spent with no write. This is a real serialization point, not a probabilistic one -- TEST-DESIGNER's 20+-repeat concurrency test is meaningful because the lock genuinely forces sequential commit ordering on this row, not because the race window happens to be too narrow to hit in practice.

3) IDENTITY-LEAKAGE TRADEOFF -- re-verified independently, not taken on the design doc's word. Read schema.ts line 361 directly: `uniqueIndex("invite_codes_code_unique").on(table.code)` -- the code column is genuinely unique-indexed, and getInviteCodeByCode's lookup (inviteCode.ts:518-538) is a plain `eq(inviteCodes.code, code)` exact-string match, not a prefix/fuzzy match, not a hash comparison with a timing side-channel of note (a DB index lookup, not a bespoke comparison loop). generateInviteCode (inviteCode.ts:48-55) draws INVITE_CODE_LENGTH=26 characters from a 32-symbol alphabet via node:crypto randomBytes with an unbiased mod-32 mapping (256/32 exactly divides, confirmed no modulo bias) -- 26*5=130 bits of entropy, clearing S4's >=128-bit floor with a 2-bit margin. Reaching the not-yours branch requires the caller to already possess the exact 26-character code string (the unique index makes a partial/near match impossible to leverage), which at 130 bits is computationally infeasible to guess. The distinct not-yours vs not-found message therefore discloses nothing beyond "this exact string, which the caller already had, is a real personal code" -- consistent with the requirement's own explicit demand for five distinct refusal reasons (issue text, AC3) and this design's stated resolution. Independently confirmed correct, not merely cited.

4) S1 CONSENT PRECEDES STORAGE -- traced resolveInviteDeepLink (start.ts, new function) statement by statement. First statement: `if (!hasConsented) { ...ctx.reply(consent prompt)...; return; }` -- this is the FIRST line of the function body; no `getInviteCodeByCode`, no `redeemInviteCode`, no db read/write of any kind precedes it. Only after this guard does `redeemInviteCode` get called. Traced the call site in makeStartHandler (start.ts ~line 497-511): the `payload.kind === "invite"` branch passes `flowUser.consentPdAt !== null` as `hasConsented` -- so an unconsented user's tap on `?start=i_<code>` reaches resolveInviteDeepLink with hasConsented=false, sends the consent prompt, and returns -- zero invite_codes/registrations/profiles I/O. The only DB write that happens before this point in the whole /start flow is `resolveOrCreateUser` (line 449), which writes only the `users` row (tg_id/tg_username/lang) -- this is pre-existing REQ-014/016 baseline behavior for EVERY /start path (event, checkin, invite, plain), not something this requirement introduces, and it is not a Profile write and not gated by consent_pd_at by design (S1's table only requires consent before `Profile`/personal-data storage, not before the bot's own bookkeeping row that lets it recognize the tg_id again). Resume path (consent:agree callback, makeConsentCallbackHandler's new `else if (payload.kind === "invite")` branch) calls resolveInviteDeepLink with hasConsented=true only AFTER recordConsent has already committed -- confirmed by its position in the diff (same branch structure as the pre-existing "event" sibling, called after the consent-recording call above it in the same function). No path exists where redeemInviteCode executes before consent_pd_at is set.

5) S7 CAPACITY STILL HOLDS -- decideRegistrationOutcome's table (registration.ts:64-93) is called identically by both registerForEvent and redeemInviteCode, and its row 5 (`requiresInvite && !inviteSatisfied -> requires-invite`) is a STRICT PREFIX of rows 6-8 (approval/admitted/waitlisted) in the first-match-wins order -- a code that clears row 5 (inviteSatisfied:true, passed by construction at redeemInviteCode step 8) falls straight into row 7/8, which read `seatsLeft` computed from the SAME locked-event admittedCount as the plain path (redeemInviteCode step 7, inviteCode.ts:719-723, identical shape to registerForEvent's own step 4). There is no branch anywhere in redeemInviteCode that sets outcome to "admitted" directly or bypasses the seatsLeft>0 check -- capacity enforcement is structurally the same code path, not a parallel one a code could special-case around. A valid code on a full event necessarily reaches row 8 (`waitlisted`). Confirmed by reading the table and the call, not by design-doc assertion.

6) S8 AUDIT -- confirmed exactly one writeAuditLog call exists in redeemInviteCode (line 806-818), placed only in the step-10 writing-outcomes branch (reached only after outcome.kind is admitted/waitlisted/requested, i.e. only on success) and never in the step-6 refusal switch or the step-9 non-writing-outcome early return. Grepped inviteCode.ts for writeAuditLog: exactly one call site in the whole redemption path, and it is inside the same `tx` as the registrations write and the used_count UPDATE -- same transaction, same commit boundary, satisfying "exactly one row, same transaction as the write." No second `invite_code.redeem` row is written anywhere (confirmed absent from the diff) -- the design's own stated resolution (traceability via payload.inviteCodeId on the single registration.* row) is what's actually implemented, not merely documented.

7) NO SECOND CODE GENERATOR / NO SCHEMA CHANGE / NO WISHLIST -- `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` and `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/drizzle` are both empty (re-ran independently, zero output) -- no migration, no new column on events/users/any table. generateInviteCode (inviteCode.ts:48-55, REQ-033's existing function) is the only CSPRNG code generator in this diff; redeemInviteCode never generates a code, only validates/consumes one. `grep -ril wishlist apps/bot/src` hits only pre-existing, untouched files (organizerRequests.ts, registrationApproval.db.test.ts) that are not in this diff's changed-file list -- confirmed via git diff --stat above.

All seven items check out under independent re-derivation. No defect found. AC2 and AC4, the two highest-stakes properties named for this gate, both hold structurally (not probabilistically) under the exact negative/concurrency scenarios constructed by hand against the real control flow.
